feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: the s-bend lead is the main lever. Iteration 2 (y = 0.04) and iteration 5 (y = 0.06) both gave s-bend progress 0.04. Iteration 3 (y = 0.07, mass 0.8) gave 0.165 and iteration 6 (y = 0.07, mass 0.6) gave 0.1625. That is a threshold between 0.06 and 0.07, so the gain is not linear and y = 0.08 could overshoot. Oscillation is the cost. Iteration 3 had s-bend steering_oscillation 0.144 and iteration 6 had 0.140, both under the 0.15 limit. Iteration 4 showed that a narrower track raises oscillation (0.164), so you should expect the stronger lead to add oscillation as well. Integration note: the controller is unchanged (kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction, weights 25 times x). A longer lead gives the controller earlier information, so I expect less lag rather than a gain change. Oval progress has stayed at 0.115 to 0.1175 in every race, so it is not the lever to chase at y = 0.08. Decide the next step from the per-track telemetry: if the s-bend progress rises above 0.1625 with s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.15, and slalom line losses stay at or below one per run, keep y = 0.08. If the oscillation exceeds 0.15, the lead is past the useful range.
requested_changes: If the next race shows s-bend progress above 0.1625 with s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.15 and slalom line losses at or below 1.0 at y = 0.08 and mass 0.6, keep y = 0.08 and mass 0.6. Evidence: the lead moved s-bend progress from 0.04 (y = 0.06) to 0.165 (y = 0.07), so a further lead is the next s-bend gain to keep.

If the next race shows s-bend steering_oscillation above 0.15 at y = 0.08, restore y = 0.07 with mass 0.6 and test y = 0.075 as the single change. Evidence: iteration 3 at y = 0.07 had s-bend oscillation 0.144, and iteration 4 at a narrower track had 0.164, so the limit is close to the 0.07 to 0.08 range, and an intermediate lead tests where the oscillation crosses 0.15.

If the next race shows slalom line losses above 1.0 or slalom progress below 0.1075 at y = 0.08, restore y = 0.07 and do not raise the lead further. Evidence: the slalom had one line loss per run at y = 0.07 (iterations 3 and 6), and y = 0.06 dropped the s-bend, so the slalom losses are the next warning sign that the lead is past its useful range.
